citations.long: Separate or defined areas to prevent contamination or mix-ups are deficient regarding operations related to the holding of rejected components, drug product containers, and labeling before disposition.

citations.short: Buildings not maintained in good state of repair
citations.long: Buildings used in the manufacturing, processing, packing, and holding of a drug product are not maintained in a good state of repair.
Procedures for the cleaning and maintenance of equipment are deficient regarding inspection of the equipment for cleanliness immediately before use.
Deviations from written specifications and test procedures are not recorded and justified.
Established laboratory control mechanisms are not followed and documented at the time of performance.

Written calibration procedures for instruments, apparatus, gauges, and recording devices are deficient in that they do not include specific directions, schedules, and provisions for remedial action if limits are not met.
The written stability testing program is not followed.

citations.short: Testing in same container - closure system
citations.long: The written stability program does not assure testing of the drug product in the same container-closure system as that in which the drug product is marketed.

citations.short: Items to cover on annual reviews
citations.long: Written procedures are not established for evaluations done at least annually and including provisions for a review of complaints, recalls, returned or salvaged drug products, and investigations conducted for each drug product.

citations.short: Procedures not  in writing, fully followed
citations.long: The responsibilities and procedures applicable to the quality control unit are not in writing.
Equipment and utensils are not cleaned at appropriate intervals to prevent contamination that would alter the safety, identity, strength, quality or purity of the drug product.

citations.short: Control procedures to monitor and validate performance
citations.long: Control procedures are not established which monitor the output and validate the performance of those manufacturing processes that may be responsible for causing variability in the characteristics of in-process material and the drug product.

citations.short: Procedures not  in writing, fully followed
citations.long: The responsibilities and procedures applicable to the quality control unit are not in writing.
Equipment used in the manufacture, processing, packing or holding of drug products is not of appropriate design, of adequate size, and suitably located to facilitate operations for its intended use.
Equipment and utensils are not cleaned at appropriate intervals to prevent contamination that would alter the safety, identity, strength, quality or purity of the drug product.
Written procedures are not established and followed for the cleaning and maintenance of equipment, including utensils, used in the manufacture, processing, packing or holding of a drug product.

citations.short: Backup data not assured as exact and complete
citations.long: Backup data is not assured as exact and secure from alteration, erasure or loss through keeping hard copy or alternate systems.
Deviations from written production and process control procedures are not recorded and justified.
Deviations from written specifications and test procedures are not recorded and justified.
Established laboratory control mechanisms are not followed and documented at the time of performance.
The establishment of specifications and test procedures including any changes thereto, are not drafted by the appropriate organizational unit and reviewed and approved by the quality control unit.

Laboratory controls do not include the establishment of scientifically sound and appropriate test procedures designed to assure that in-process materials conform to appropriate standards of identity, strength, quality and purity.

citations.short: Calibration - at intervals, written program, remedial action
citations.long: The calibration of instruments is not done at suitable intervals in accordance with an established written program and with provisions for remedial action in the event accuracy and/or precision limits are not met.

Where data from accelerated studies was used to project a tentative expiration date beyond a date supported by actual shelf life studies, there were no drug product testing at appropriate intervals conducted until the tentative expiration date was verified or the appropriate expiration date determined.

citations.short: Retention time of reserve samples, in general
citations.long: Reserve samples for active ingredients and drug products are not retained for one year after the expiration date of the drug product.
Written records of investigations into the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet specifications do not always include the conclusions and follow-up.

citations.short: Data secured in course of each test
citations.long: Laboratory records do not include a complete record of all data secured in the course of each test, including all graphs, charts, and spectra from laboratory instrumentation, properly identified to show the drug product tested.
Procedures describing the handling of written and oral complaints related to drug products are deficiently written or followed.

citations.short: Prepared for each batch, include complete information
citations.long: Batch production and control records are not prepared for each batch of drug product produced.
Investigations of an unexplained discrepancy did not extend to other batches of the same drug product and other drug products that may have been associated with the specific failure or discrepancy.
